options.summary: Monolithic CLI pipeline – a single Node.js CLI application with an in-process pipeline that reads Markdown, builds a link/tag graph, renders HTML with templates, generates a client-side search index, and writes the output directory. All stages run sequentially in one process.

components.name: CLI Entry Point
responsibilities: Parse command-line arguments (source dir, output dir, config file path)
Load configuration and validate inputs
Orchestrate the build pipeline stages in order
Report errors and build summary

components.name: Markdown Ingestion Module
responsibilities: Recursively scan source directory for .md files
Read file contents and extract YAML front matter (title, tags, metadata)
Normalize file identifiers (slug from filename) for cross-referencing

components.name: Link & Tag Graph Builder
responsibilities: Parse each note's body for internal links (Markdown links and wiki-links)
Build a directed graph of note-to-note references
Compute backlinks (reverse edges) for every note
Collect and normalize tags from front matter and inline hashtags
Produce a structured NoteGraph object consumed by downstream stages

components.name: Markdown Renderer
responsibilities: Convert Markdown AST to HTML using a configurable Markdown-it (or unified/remark) pipeline
Support syntax highlighting for code blocks
Inject backlinks section and tag list into each note's HTML

components.name: Template Engine
responsibilities: Render note pages, tag index pages, home page, and all-notes page using HTML templates (e.g., Nunjucks/EJS)
Accept theme/layout configuration
Produce final HTML strings per page

components.name: Search Index Generator
responsibilities: Build a client-side search index (e.g., Lunr.js or FlexSearch) from note titles and body text
Serialize the index to a JSON file included in the output

components.name: Output Writer
responsibilities: Write generated HTML, CSS, JS, and search index to the output directory
Copy static assets (images, fonts)
Generate sitemap or manifest if configured

components.name: Client-Side Search UI
responsibilities: Load the prebuilt search index in the browser
Provide a search input with instant results overlay
Link results to note pages

interfaces.contract: Passes validated config object containing sourceDirPath, outputDirPath, and options map.
Returns NoteFile[] where each entry has slug, rawMarkdown, frontMatter (tags, title), and filePath.
Returns NoteGraph containing Map<slug, NoteNode> with fields: slug, title, tags[], outLinks[], backLinks[], rawMarkdown.
Returns RenderedNote[] each with slug, htmlContent, tags[], backLinks[], title.
Provides NoteGraph (titles + body text) for index construction.
Returns PageOutput[] each with relativePath and htmlString, plus list of static asset paths.
Returns serialized search index JSON blob to be written to output directory.
Browser loads search-index.json via HTTP GET; CMP_A8 is bundled JS included in every page.

pros: Simple to build, test, and debug as a single process
No external dependencies beyond Node.js and npm packages
Easy to distribute as a single npm package or binary
Straightforward incremental-build extension (add file-hash caching layer later)
Low latency build for small-to-medium note sets
cons: All logic coupled in one codebase; harder to swap individual stages independently
Single-threaded by default; large note sets (10k+) may see slow builds without worker threads
Tightly coupled to Node.js ecosystem; harder for non-JS developers to extend
Template and renderer choices baked in; switching requires code changes

risks: Performance may degrade with very large note collections (>5k notes) without parallelization or incremental builds
Tight coupling between graph builder and renderer may complicate future plugin architecture
Client-side search index size may become prohibitive for very large corpora, impacting page load

options.summary: Plugin-based static site generator architecture – a lightweight core orchestrator exposes a plugin API with defined hook points (ingest, transform, render, emit). Each concern (Markdown parsing, link resolution, tag extraction, search indexing, theming) is a separate plugin. Enables community/user extensibility.

components.name: Core Orchestrator
responsibilities: Load configuration and discover/register plugins
Define build lifecycle hooks: onIngest, onTransform, onRender, onEmit
Execute hooks in defined order, passing a shared BuildContext
Provide plugin API for registering hooks and accessing shared state

components.name: File Ingestion Plugin
responsibilities: Scan source directory for Markdown files
Read contents and emit NoteFile objects into BuildContext

components.name: Front Matter & Tag Plugin
responsibilities: Parse YAML front matter from each note
Extract and normalize tags (front matter + inline hashtags)
Attach metadata to each NoteFile in BuildContext

components.name: Link Resolution & Backlink Plugin
responsibilities: Detect internal links (Markdown links, wiki-links) in note bodies
Resolve link targets to note slugs
Build forward and backward link maps in BuildContext

components.name: Markdown Render Plugin
responsibilities: Convert Markdown to HTML using configurable parser (markdown-it, remark, etc.)
Apply syntax highlighting for code blocks
Store rendered HTML in BuildContext per note

components.name: Theme / Template Plugin
responsibilities: Provide HTML templates for note pages, tag pages, index pages
Render final HTML from BuildContext data using a template engine
Support user-supplied theme overrides

components.name: Search Index Plugin
responsibilities: Build client-side search index from BuildContext note data
Emit index file to output

components.name: Emit Plugin
responsibilities: Write all generated pages, assets, and index files to output directory
Handle base URL rewriting for deployment targets

components.name: Client-Side Runtime
responsibilities: Search UI: load index, render results
Backlink navigation and tag filtering in the browser

interfaces.contract: Orchestrator invokes onIngest hook; plugin writes NoteFile[] to BuildContext.notes.
Orchestrator invokes onTransform hook; plugin reads BuildContext.notes, mutates each note's metadata field in place.
Orchestrator invokes onTransform hook (after CMP_A22); plugin reads note bodies, writes BuildContext.linkGraph (Map<slug, {outLinks, backLinks}>).
Orchestrator invokes onRender hook; plugin reads rawMarkdown from BuildContext.notes, writes htmlContent per note.
Orchestrator invokes onRender hook (after CMP_A24); plugin reads htmlContent, linkGraph, tags and produces final PageOutput[] in BuildContext.pages.
Orchestrator invokes onRender hook; plugin reads BuildContext.notes titles/bodies and writes searchIndex blob to BuildContext.assets.
Orchestrator invokes onEmit hook; plugin reads BuildContext.pages and BuildContext.assets, writes to disk.
Static files served to browser; CMP_A28 fetches search-index.json at runtime.

pros: Highly extensible: users and contributors can add/replace plugins without modifying core
Separation of concerns makes individual plugins easier to test in isolation
Supports multiple Markdown flavors and template engines via plugin swap
Community can contribute plugins (e.g., graph visualization, RSS feed)
Easier to implement incremental builds as a plugin
cons: Higher upfront design and implementation effort for the plugin API
Plugin ordering and inter-plugin dependencies add complexity
Debugging build issues may be harder due to indirection through hooks
Potential performance overhead from hook dispatch and shared mutable BuildContext
Requires good documentation for plugin authors

risks: Plugin API design may need breaking changes as new use cases emerge, causing ecosystem churn
Shared mutable BuildContext can lead to subtle bugs if plugins mutate state unexpectedly
Plugin discovery and version compatibility management adds maintenance burden

options.summary: Python-based CLI with decoupled processing stages – uses Python (with libraries like markdown-it-py or mistune for Markdown, Jinja2 for templates, and Whoosh or a custom inverted-index builder for search). Each stage is a standalone Python module invoked by a CLI driver. Targets users already in a Python ecosystem.

components.name: CLI Driver (Click/Typer)
responsibilities: Parse CLI arguments and load YAML/TOML config
Orchestrate pipeline: ingest → graph → render → search → emit
Provide watch mode via filesystem polling or watchdog library
Report build statistics and errors

components.name: Ingestion Module
responsibilities: Walk source directory tree for .md files
Parse YAML front matter using python-frontmatter
Return list of NoteRecord dataclass instances

components.name: Graph Module
responsibilities: Scan note bodies for internal links (regex + AST-based detection)
Build networkx or custom adjacency-list graph
Compute backlinks via graph transpose
Extract and normalize tags

components.name: Render Module
responsibilities: Convert Markdown to HTML (markdown-it-py / mistune)
Inject backlinks and tag sections into note HTML
Support code syntax highlighting via Pygments

components.name: Template Module
responsibilities: Use Jinja2 to render page layouts (note, tag index, home, all-notes)
Accept user-provided template overrides directory
Generate navigation and breadcrumb HTML

components.name: Search Index Builder
responsibilities: Tokenize and stem note text
Build a JSON search index compatible with Lunr.js (via lunr.py or custom builder)
Write index to output directory

components.name: Output Emitter
responsibilities: Write HTML pages, CSS, JS, and search index to output directory
Copy static assets
Optionally run post-processing (HTML minification)

components.name: Client-Side Search UI
responsibilities: Load Lunr.js index in browser
Render search results with links to note pages

interfaces.contract: CLI calls ingest(source_dir: Path) → List[NoteRecord] where NoteRecord has slug, raw_md, front_matter dict, file_path.
Graph module receives List[NoteRecord], returns NoteGraph dataclass with nodes dict and edges (forward_links, back_links per slug), plus tags_map: Dict[tag, List[slug]].
Render module receives NoteGraph, returns List[RenderedNote] with slug, html_content, tags, back_links.
Template module receives List[RenderedNote] plus tags_map and site config, returns List[PageOutput] with relative_path and html_string.
Search builder receives List[NoteRecord] (titles + bodies), outputs search_index.json bytes.
Emitter receives List[PageOutput] and search_index bytes, writes all to output_dir.
Browser fetches search-index.json; CMP_A37 is bundled JS served with the site.

pros: Leverages rich Python ecosystem (markdown-it-py, Jinja2, Pygments, networkx)
Familiar to users who already use Python-based tooling
Jinja2 templates are widely known and easy to customize
Easy to package as a pip-installable CLI tool
networkx provides robust graph operations for backlink analysis
cons: Python build performance is slower than Node.js for large file I/O and string processing
Client-side search still requires JavaScript, so the project spans two languages
Smaller ecosystem for static-site-specific tooling compared to Node.js
Watch mode and live reload require additional libraries (watchdog + livereload)
Distribution as a standalone binary is harder than with Node.js (requires pyinstaller or similar)

risks: Python Markdown libraries may not support all GFM extensions out of the box, requiring custom plugins
Generating a Lunr.js-compatible index from Python requires careful compatibility testing
Build times for 1000+ notes may be noticeably slower than Node.js alternatives without multiprocessing

options.summary: Extend an existing SSG (e.g., Eleventy/11ty) via custom plugins and data pipeline – rather than building from scratch, configure Eleventy as the core engine and implement backlinks, tag pages, and search as Eleventy plugins and data files. Minimizes custom code by leveraging a battle-tested SSG.

components.name: Eleventy Core (External Dependency)
responsibilities: Provide static site generation engine with template rendering, collections, and pagination
Handle file watching and dev server
Process Markdown files with configurable Markdown library

components.name: Eleventy Configuration Module
responsibilities: Define .eleventy.js configuration: input/output dirs, Markdown library setup, template formats
Register custom collections (allNotes, taggedNotes)
Register shortcodes and filters for backlinks and tag rendering

components.name: Backlinks Data Plugin
responsibilities: Run as an Eleventy beforeBuild event handler or computed data function
Scan all note content for internal links (wiki-links and Markdown links)
Compute backlinks map and inject into each note's data cascade

components.name: Tag Pages Generator
responsibilities: Use Eleventy pagination to auto-generate a page per tag
Provide tag index page listing all tags with counts
Leverage Eleventy's built-in tags collection with custom filtering

components.name: Search Index Build Step
responsibilities: Implement as an Eleventy afterBuild event or a custom transform
Read rendered content, tokenize, and build a Lunr.js / Pagefind index
Write index file(s) to output directory

components.name: Theme / Layout Templates
responsibilities: Provide Nunjucks/Liquid templates for note page, tag page, home page, all-notes page
Include search UI component in base layout
Style with CSS (custom or a CSS framework)

components.name: Client-Side Runtime
responsibilities: Search UI using Lunr.js or Pagefind JS widget
Interactive backlink/tag navigation

interfaces.contract: Configuration module exports a function that receives eleventyConfig and registers plugins, collections, filters, and shortcodes.
Plugin registers eleventyConfig.addGlobalData('backlinks', async () => backlinksMap) or uses computed data; Eleventy merges into template data.
Tag pages defined as a template with pagination: { data: 'collections', size: 1, alias: 'tag' }; Eleventy generates one page per tag.
Registers eleventyConfig.on('eleventy.after', async () => buildSearchIndex(outputDir)); writes search-index.json to output.
Eleventy passes merged data (note content, backlinks, tags, collections) to templates; templates render final HTML.
Generated static files served to browser; CMP_A46 JS loaded in pages fetches search index.

pros: Minimal custom code; leverages Eleventy's mature, well-documented SSG features
Built-in dev server, watch mode, and incremental builds out of the box
Large community and plugin ecosystem for additional features (RSS, sitemap, image optimization)
Battle-tested Markdown processing and template rendering
Easy to adopt Pagefind for search (zero-config, excellent performance)
cons: Tightly coupled to Eleventy's architecture and release cycle
Wiki-link support and backlinks require custom logic not native to Eleventy
Less control over build internals; debugging may require understanding Eleventy's data cascade
Harder to distribute as a standalone tool; users must install Node.js and npm dependencies
Eleventy version upgrades may break custom plugins

risks: Eleventy API changes in major versions could break backlinks plugin and custom configuration
Wiki-link parsing in Markdown-it requires a community plugin (markdown-it-wikilinks) that may lag behind or be unmaintained
Pagefind or Lunr.js integration as a post-build step may not cover all search requirements without customization
Users unfamiliar with Eleventy's data cascade may find customization confusing
